newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed broadly higher on Wednesday amid heavy trading by institutional investors, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.09 pct to 102.77
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 101.70.
Volume was a high 205 million shekels.

"Bond prices rose amid high activity of institutional investors. Yields on inflation-linked bonds are getting closer to 4.0 percent, which is still attractive for these investors," said Baruch Glicksberg of Clal Insurance.

"Yields on CPI-linked bonds fell to 4.17 percent but institutional invstors continue to buy. I believe that yields will fall in the near future to only 3.8 percent," said Gidi Halperin of Meitav Securities and Investments.
Traders noted that medium-term CPI-linked bonds were today's main gainers.

Unlinked bonds also rose, which traders said reflected expectations of lower interest rates. "The government is showing that it is committed to fiscal discipline. Eventually the central bank will be forced to lower its key lending rate," Glicksberg said.
Traders said dollar-linked bonds posted only mild gains today despite the decline of the shekel against the U.S. currency.
On Wednesday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3220 shekels against 3.3160 shekels on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
